notes: Only n_o and es_value_o were assigned; replication, original p, and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Target ambiguity: the article has 12 language studies, plus combined analyses, and Figure 2 on the supplied p.11 locator shows four contrasts. The source does not identify a numbered Study 1 selecting a unique language/sample/test. Candidate final participant total is explicitly printed as 2047 after mother-tongue exclusions; it is not assigned as the target analytic N. Table 2 gives sample-specific participant candidates: Dutch 277, English 212, Finnish 119, French 294, German 247, Greek 86, Hungarian 78, Italian 257, Norwegian 37, Polish 137, Portuguese 106, Spanish 197. These are separate samples, not alternative estimates of one test N. No arithmetic N derivation performed. The primary randomization unit is the letter-specific own/not-own preference-proportion difference, with never-name letters excluded. Printed full-name combined descriptive candidates on p.390 are probabilities 0.20 (not-own) and 0.30 (own), described as 50 per cent more likely; no subtraction, ratio computation, standardization or d conversion performed. Other printed combined descriptive candidates are 0.33 versus 0.20 for first-name letters (pp.391–392), 0.28 versus 0.20 for family-name letters (p.392), and 0.46 versus 0.21 for initials (p.392). Figure 2 separately plots each language and contrast; no graph coordinates were estimated. These cannot uniquely fill one scalar es_value_o. PDF p.11 was rendered and inspected at /home/lukas/.cache/fred-completion-renders/276bac1e9e0859a0/page11.png. Quotes use the supplied canonical text literally.
